clue.text: Exclusive group about to provide secret information, we are told

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the leaking word stands for how it sounds

parts.note: to leak is to pass on confidential material

explanation.surface: A tight little circle is about to spill its secrets, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus LEAK, said together, sounds like the French-derived word for a closed set of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small, select circle of people who keep outsiders away.

clue.text: Family business

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... of descent, as in coming from a noble ...
second meaning: a trade or occupation

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a family firm; the two words are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ancestry or lineage and a branch of trade one works in.

clue.text: Putting out that the heartless monarch's feeling sore, but not at first

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so losing it drops the middle of the royal title

parts.note: a queen is a female monarch; the 's here reads as 'is'

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for feeling sore is left off

parts.note: aching describes a dull pain

explanation.surface: Something being extinguished while a sorrowful, rather empty-hearted ruler feels pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Quenching a fire or a light is extinguishing it, the same as putting it out.

clue.text: Fears losing head, so blunders

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: terrors are intense fears

explanation.surface: Someone frightened out of their wits ends up making mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors and blunders are both mistakes, plural nouns for things done wrongly.

clue.text: Experts in consumerism

definitions.meaning: read literally as the business of consuming, that is eating and drinking well

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to shopping and the economy; the real consumers here are those who relish fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmets are connoisseurs of good food and drink, people expert in what they consume.

clue.text: A parting gesture from Midas?

definitions.meaning: a farewell shake of the hand, or a generous payoff on leaving a job
King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his handshake would be golden

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a large severance payment is read literally as the touch of the king of Greek legend whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a generous lump sum given to a departing executive, a lavish farewell.

clue.text: Hoofed out gun you reportedly found old

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the weapon are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the pronoun, said aloud, is the name of the letter U
late can mean former or deceased

explanation.surface: Someone kicked out a gun that, it is said, you found to be old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoofed out' reads as a phrase for kicked out, but only 'Hoofed' is the definition; 'out' works on the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungulate is a hoofed mammal, and the word is also an adjective meaning having hooves.

clue.text: Doctor chap's a fool

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
Ron stands for any man's name; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A physician's friend turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is an insulting word for a stupid person, a dunce.

clue.text: Chase it back around to the headland in a bad temper

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes around the engraving word
back means the short word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
to chase metal is to engrave it, so etch
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone in a foul mood pursues a thing back round to a cliff top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' looks like pursue, but in metalwork it means engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchiness is irritability, a peevish ill humour.

clue.text: Whole triangle shaken

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled, so the letters of the shape are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A percussion triangle being rattled in its entirety.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means complete or entire, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Turn round at borders of Germany and tear off

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong, so the letters of the rip are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to wheel about at the German frontier and dash away.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or spin in a circle.

clue.text: Complete discretion gives Albert chance to spin

indicators.note: spinning whirls the letters of the two words into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Total freedom lets a man named Albert have a go at spinning something.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche is French for a blank card: unlimited authority to act as one sees fit.

clue.text: Joining the union again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
marriage is the joining of two people in wedlock, the union of the clue

explanation.surface: A worker signing up to a trade union once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it; the wedding sense of union hides behind the trade union one.
explanation.definitionFit: A remarriage is a second wedding, entering the marital union anew.

clue.text: Not the house for those of a detached frame of mind

definitions.meaning: points to a type of British home

definitions.text: for those of a detached frame of mind
definitions.meaning: a detached house stands alone, unlike one that is only half detached

explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house in Britain, joined to its neighbour on one side, so anyone wanting a detached home would turn it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The short British word names a house sharing one wall with the next.

clue.text: Top clothing here — and that's strange

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged, so these are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Pointing to a place to put hats, then remarking how odd it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a pole with pegs for hanging headwear, so where clothing for the head goes.

clue.text: These transactions start with a ringing endorsement

definitions.meaning: deals or sales of some kind
a ringing endorsement is normally a hearty recommendation, but here the ringing is of a phone

explanation.walkthrough: These sales begin with a call ringing at the customer's end, not with enthusiastic praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Telesales are goods sold by telephone, with the seller cold-calling buyers.

clue.text: Something spicy for an evil sounding person at the start of the week

indicators.note: sounding means the word is replaced by letters said the same way

parts.note: evil ... person, split around the sound signal, is a sinner, a wrongdoer
Mon is short for Monday, the week's first working day

explanation.surface: Something racy for a villain-like figure first thing on Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'evil' and 'person' together give the wrongdoer, with 'sounding' placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a fragrant spice taken from tree bark.

clue.text: Nerve centre of group seeking new oil supply

parts.note: a gang is a band of people

indicators.note: read as supple-y, bendy, so the letters of the fuel are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The headquarters of a cartel hunting for fresh petroleum reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but works as an adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a mass of nerve cells, literally a nerve centre in anatomy.

clue.text: Left first catalogue

parts.note: 1st is the short form of first, read as I-S-T

explanation.surface: An instruction that the left-hand item comes first in a register.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is an itemised record, the same as a catalogue.

clue.text: Tackles the beavers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: confronts boldly, as to beard someone in their den
second meaning: beaver is old slang for a beard

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone grappling with the animals; both words are senses of one plural word.
explanation.definitionFit: To beard someone is to challenge them face to face, and beaver was once slang for a man's facial hair.

clue.text: What the ice cream vendor has in store?

definitions.text: What the ice cream vendor has

definitions.meaning: things kept in stock, but also the phrase for unrealisable capital

explanation.walkthrough: The financial term for funds that cannot be drawn on is read literally as the chilled stock in an ice cream seller's freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen assets are holdings that cannot be sold or used, here pictured as stock kept icy cold.

clue.text: Unknown for one daughter to be confined to the area

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities
one is a single instance, taken as written

explanation.surface: An unidentified person tells a daughter she must stay within the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that is zoned has been designated for a particular use within a set district.

clue.text: Caught in uncle's scandal

indicators.note: in puts the cricket letter inside the uncle's name

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is implicated in a family scandal involving their uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or fraud, a disgraceful racket of the kind that causes scandal.

clue.text: In sabotaging the AGM, the miners show bottle

indicators.note: sabotage wrecks the meeting, so its letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

explanation.surface: Coal miners disrupt the annual general meeting and display their courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for nerve, which makes 'show bottle' read as showing courage; here it is the noun for a large wine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine or champagne bottle twice the standard size.

clue.text: Cry about short girl's fabrics

indicators.note: the shortened name with its 's goes about the word for weep
short means a letter is cut from the name

parts.note: Alice stands for any girl, with the possessive S kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wails over a little girl's textiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylics are synthetic textiles woven from acrylic fibres.

clue.text: Only half the cha-cha steps at afternoon function

parts.note: half of the dance's name is cha, British slang for tea
a dance is a sequence of steps

explanation.surface: At an afternoon party, they only manage half the Latin dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is an old British slang word for tea, from the Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea dance is an afternoon social gathering with tea and dancing.

clue.text: Seems a funny source of oil

indicators.note: funny means peculiar, so the letters are rearranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An observation that something appears to be a strange origin of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to yield sesame oil, used widely in cooking.
